title: Quiz 5 Review - Divide and Conquer Algorithms
notes: Divide and conquer algorithms solve problems by recursively dividing them into smaller subproblems of the same type.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
Each divide-and-conquer algorithm has three steps: divide, conquer, and combine.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
The efficiency of divide-and-conquer algorithms can be analyzed using recurrence relations.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
The Master Theorem provides a general solution for divide-and-conquer recurrence relations of the form T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
In the Master Theorem, 'a' is the number of subproblems, 'b' is the division factor, and 'f(n)' is the cost of dividing and combining.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
If f(n) = O(n^c) and a < b^c, then T(n) = Θ(n^c) (Case 1 of the Master Theorem).
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
If f(n) = Θ(n^{log_b a}), then T(n) = Θ(n^{log_b a} log n) (Case 2 of the Master Theorem).
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
If f(n) = Ω(n^c) and a > b^c, then T(n) = Θ(n^{log_b a}) (Case 3 of the Master Theorem).
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
MergeSort splits an array into halves, recursively sorts them, and merges the results.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
MergeSort has a time complexity of Θ(n log n) and requires O(n) extra space.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
QuickSort selects a pivot, partitions the array, and recursively sorts the partitions.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
The average time complexity of QuickSort is O(n log n), but the worst case is O(n²) if pivots are unbalanced.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
The partition step in QuickSort ensures that all elements less than the pivot are on its left and greater ones on the right.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
Choosing a good pivot is essential to avoid worst-case performance in QuickSort.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
A tree is a connected acyclic graph with one root node.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
In a binary search tree (BST), all left child keys are smaller and all right child keys are larger than the parent key.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
BST operations include insert, delete, and search, each having O(h) complexity where h is the tree height.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
BST traversals can be in-order, pre-order, or post-order.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
In-order traversal of a BST visits nodes in sorted order.
Week 5 - Divide and Conquer.pdf
Karatsuba's algorithm improves integer multiplication to O(n^{log2(3)}) ≈ O(n^{1.585}) using divide-and-conquer.

flashcards.front: What are the three steps of a divide-and-conquer algorithm?
flashcards.back: Divide, Conquer, and Combine.

flashcards.front: What is the general recurrence relation for divide-and-conquer algorithms?
flashcards.back: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).

flashcards.front: What does 'a' represent in the Master Theorem?
flashcards.back: The number of subproblems the problem is divided into.

flashcards.front: What does 'b' represent in the Master Theorem?
flashcards.back: The factor by which the problem size is reduced in each subproblem.

flashcards.front: What does 'f(n)' represent in the Master Theorem?
flashcards.back: The non-recursive cost (divide and combine work).

flashcards.front: What is the base case of MergeSort?
flashcards.back: When the list contains only one element.

flashcards.front: What is MergeSort’s time complexity?
flashcards.back: Θ(n log n).

flashcards.front: What is QuickSort’s average time complexity?
flashcards.back: O(n log n).

flashcards.front: What is QuickSort’s worst-case time complexity?
flashcards.back: O(n²), occurring when partitions are unbalanced.

flashcards.front: Why is MergeSort not in-place?
flashcards.back: It requires O(n) extra space to store temporary arrays during merging.

flashcards.front: What is the advantage of QuickSort over MergeSort?
flashcards.back: QuickSort is in-place and often faster on average due to cache efficiency.

flashcards.front: What determines QuickSort’s efficiency?
flashcards.back: The choice of the pivot element.

flashcards.front: What is the key property of a binary search tree?
flashcards.back: All keys in the left subtree are smaller, and those in the right are larger.

flashcards.front: What is the time complexity of search in a balanced BST?
flashcards.back: O(log n).

flashcards.front: What are the three depth-first traversals of a BST?
flashcards.back: In-order, Pre-order, and Post-order.

flashcards.front: What traversal outputs BST nodes in sorted order?
flashcards.back: In-order traversal.

flashcards.front: What is Karatsuba’s multiplication algorithm used for?
flashcards.back: Multiplying large integers faster than the traditional O(n²) approach.

flashcards.front: What is Karatsuba’s time complexity?
What does the Master Theorem help determine?
flashcards.back: The asymptotic runtime of divide-and-conquer algorithms.

flashcards.front: What type of data structure is used for tree traversal?
flashcards.back: A recursive call stack or explicit stack data structure.

quiz.question: What are the three main steps of a divide-and-conquer algorithm?
quiz.explanation: Divide-and-conquer algorithms divide the problem, solve subproblems, and combine results.

quiz.question: What is the general form of a divide-and-conquer recurrence?
quiz.explanation: The Master Theorem applies to recurrences of the form T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).

quiz.question: In the Master Theorem, what does 'a' represent?
quiz.explanation: 'a' is the number of subproblems created at each step.

quiz.question: What is MergeSort’s worst-case time complexity?
quiz.explanation: MergeSort always runs in Θ(n log n) time regardless of input order.

quiz.question: What is QuickSort’s worst-case time complexity?
quiz.explanation: QuickSort degrades to O(n²) when pivots cause highly unbalanced partitions.

quiz.question: What is QuickSort’s average-case complexity?
quiz.explanation: With balanced partitions, QuickSort averages O(n log n).

quiz.question: What is the base case for MergeSort recursion?
quiz.explanation: When the array size is 1, it is already sorted.

quiz.question: What is the main difference between MergeSort and QuickSort?
options: MergeSort is in-place; QuickSort is not
QuickSort is in-place; MergeSort is not
quiz.explanation: QuickSort sorts in place; MergeSort requires extra space.

quiz.question: What traversal of a BST visits nodes in sorted order?
quiz.explanation: In-order traversal visits nodes from smallest to largest.

quiz.question: What property defines a binary search tree?
options: All nodes are sorted by insertion order
quiz.explanation: BST property ensures left subtree keys < root < right subtree keys.

quiz.question: What is the time complexity of searching in a balanced BST?
quiz.explanation: A balanced BST has height log n, leading to O(log n) search time.

quiz.question: What is the key idea behind Karatsuba’s algorithm?
options: Using divide-and-conquer to reduce multiplication count
Using lookup tables for faster addition
quiz.explanation: Karatsuba uses divide-and-conquer to perform fewer multiplications than the traditional method.
